If you think this is a picture of a marathon runner coming to the end of a marathon, you are quite right. It is our new marathon record holder Lionel Mann, obviously not superstitious.

The 5¾-miles championship field, still hunched after one mile. Front row: Pat O'Connor (12), Tony Fairclough (21), Peter Carton (19), Trevor Hart (23), and Lionel Mann (9). The three framed heads look like those of Chris Steer, John Thresher and Dereck Fernee.

MANN SUPREME - CHEF RUNS OFF WITH AWARD. Marathon champion Lionel Mann, the Galloping Cordon Bleu, being presented with the "Mitchell Trophy" for the first Belgrave Harrier home in the "Poly Marathon". The "Mitchell Trophy"is being awarded by the donor of this magnificent shield, Bert Mitchell of 32, Manor Road, Deal. Bert was formerly a fierce competitor and still remains a staunch Belgrave Harrier.
The ceremony was conducted at the 21st Annual 20 Mile Road Race at Wimbledon where Lionel also ran a blistering 1hr 54 minutes for the course.
Bottom right: 'A' team regular - Lionel Mann.
Wild man of the woods? Lionel Mann on his way to second place in the Club 10 miles cross country championship.

The 10,000 metre championship for the "Tom Carter" Cup. Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best. Top right: Second-placer Colin Pearson. Bottom left: A rare appearance on the track for Stuart Masterson, here leading Keith Duckett and junior Richard Dorman. Bottom right: Steve Williams, who in his first season of track athletics has raced over all distances from 200 to 10,000 metres.
Front Cover: The harrier season is over but Lionel Mann shows signs of picking up some of his old form in good time for a season on the roads.
Back Page: Two of Belgrave's long serving stalwarts. Laurie O'Hara hands over to Lionel Mann during the 100 x 1 mile relay.

Lionel leads Bob Smith, Dick Piotrowski, and Adrian Major during the Belgrave 7½ miles Cross Country Championship of 1968 but all four had to give way to Tony Fairclough (1st), Laurie O'Hara (2nd) and Pat O'Connor (3rd) by the finish. The field was 36 strong.
